title: Don't Ship Skills Without Evals — Philipp Schmid, Google DeepMind
talk_summary: Philipp Schmid argues that agent skills (SKILL.md folders with progressive disclosure) are widely shipped without evals, and that AI-generated skills can degrade performance while human-written ones help. He shows a lightweight eval harness (JSON test cases + regex asserts + optional LLM judge) run on every skill change, with trigger/no-trigger cases and ablation runs to decide when to retire a skill.

takeaways.technique: Skill eval harness with trigger/no-trigger cases
takeaways.what_they_do: Each skill ships with a JSON/YAML file of test cases: a prompt, language, a should_trigger flag, and expected asserts; a small Python script runs the agent harness and checks outcomes.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we have a should trigger. That's basically there to tell us if the agent should read the skill or not read the skill
takeaways.numbers: 117 test cases for the Interactions API skill; ~90% valid-code rate after

takeaways.technique: Regex/script asserts instead of LLM judge by default
takeaways.what_they_do: Most skill evals are cheap deterministic checks (correct SDK, correct model ID, correct method, no old patterns) rather than LLM-as-judge; LLM judge reserved for complex trace-level checks with a rubric.
takeaways.evidence_quote: most of the tests or evals for skills can be regex

takeaways.technique: Ablation: eval with and without the skill to decide retirement
takeaways.what_they_do: Run the same eval suite with the skill enabled and disabled; if the model passes without it, retire the skill and keep the eval as a regression guard.
takeaways.evidence_quote: always try to run evals with and without the skill enabled

takeaways.what_they_do: Keep the always-loaded description to 1-2 directive sentences; put detail in a short body and push environment-specific detail (AWS vs GCP) into reference files the model reads only when needed.
takeaways.evidence_quote: skills.md files should be below 500 lines of words

takeaways.technique: Kill no-ops and prefer scripts over step-by-step skills
takeaways.what_they_do: Remove instructions that don't change behavior ('write clean code') and replace fixed workflows with scripts the model invokes, defining goals/constraints instead of exact steps.
takeaways.evidence_quote: AI generated skills tend to include a lot of no-ops

takeaways.technique: Isolated workspaces + multiple trials per case
takeaways.what_they_do: Run each eval in a clean workspace so the agent can't read prior chats/executions and cheat, and run 2-6 trials per case to measure reliability given non-determinism.
takeaways.evidence_quote: coding agents are very good at finding or cheating
